objective: Audit and repair every platform fault that made the governed cognitive turn fail with the masked code COGNITIVE_ORCHESTRATOR_UNAVAILABLE on three consecutive Founder submissions of the Certification Test One objective, using a disciplined reproduction loop instead of guesswork. Root causes found and repaired, each with evidence: ONE, error masking at two layers - the Core orchestrator collapsed every non-contract error to the safe code without recording the cause, and the gateway reported curl exit 28 (its own timeout) as DIALOGUE_PROVIDER_REJECTED, so a timeout was indistinguishable from a rejection. TWO, the gpt-oss:20b profile pinned the model to CPU with num_gpu 0; its measured load alone took 265 seconds against a 240 second budget, so every research-review call timed out deterministically; the identical request on GPU completed in 24 seconds. THREE, num_predict 2048 shared the completion budget with the model's thinking and could return empty content; raised to 6144 with the timeout at 600 seconds for CPU-fallback headroom. FOUR, capability-resolved purpose lost to keyword inference twice - Core enforceRoutePolicy re-labelled a capability-routed inspection and nulled the reviewer (COGNITIVE_REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE), and the Command Center planner did the same so the delegation envelope disagreed with the route (COGNITIVE_ROUTE_MISMATCH). Both now resolve the controller's capabilities first. FIVE, the capability-purpose table listed repository.inspect first, so a mixed coding grant collapsed to the reporting role; mutating capabilities now take precedence. The full Test One objective now completes end to end through a throwaway gateway with scratch credentials: research-review route, gpt-oss:20b specialist, qwen3.6:27b reviewer, 59 seconds.
